sections.description: Walks through the patient’s timeline from semaglutide exposure to progressive proximal weakness, highlighting the key clinical features that prompted evaluation for an inflammatory myopathy.
subtopics: Baseline comorbidities: obesity, NAFLD, HTN, hypothyroidism; prior liver workup and biopsy
Semaglutide initiation (0.25 mg SC) and immediate GI intolerance with AKI/metabolic acidosis
Early labs during first hospitalization: modest CK elevation without rhabdomyolysis features
Subacute 4-month progression: dysphagia, dysphonia, profound proximal weakness, functional decline
Second hospitalization: CK ~4000 U/L, no rash, no synovitis; new paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with normal troponin
Initial treatment at outside hospital: pulse methylprednisolone; transfer for rheumatology evaluation

sections.description: Provides focused background on immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM), contrasts it with toxic/drug-induced rhabdomyolysis, and situates GLP-1 receptor agonists as potential triggers.
subtopics: IMNM overview: clinicopathologic entity with aggressive proximal weakness, high CK, myofiber necrosis with paucity of lymphocytes
Serologic subsets: anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP; frequency and implications of seronegative IMNM
Drug-associated IMNM paradigm: statins as precedent; persistence after drug cessation and response to immunosuppression
Rhabdomyolysis vs IMNM: time course, CK dynamics, symptoms (myalgia, pigmenturia), and resolution with drug withdrawal
GLP-1 receptor agonists: common adverse effects; reports of muscle mass loss and rare rhabdomyolysis; hypothesised immune or metabolic mechanisms in susceptible hosts

Key alternative diagnoses considered: endocrine myopathies (hypothyroid ruled out), inflammatory myopathies (dermatomyositis, overlap syndromes), neuromuscular junction disorders, critical illness myopathy, hepatic vs muscle sources of transaminases, myocarditis vs stress cardiomyopathy

sections.description: Details the investigations and explains how data converged on seronegative IMNM probably associated with semaglutide, while excluding competing causes.
subtopics: Laboratory evaluation: rising CK to ~4000 U/L; ESR/CRP elevation; normal TSH; AST/ALT elevation in the context of known NAFLD; isolated low-titre SS-B
Autoantibody testing: negative ANA and comprehensive myositis panel including anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP; implications of seronegativity
Muscle MRI: symmetric thigh muscle edema supporting inflammatory myopathy
Cardiac assessment: echo and cardiac MRI showing transient edema/hypokinesis without scar—consider early myocarditis vs stress-induced cardiomyopathy; normalization on follow-up
Muscle biopsy: necrotic/regenerating fibers, macrophage-rich myophagocytosis (CD68), membrane attack complex on myofibers, rare CD3+ cells—pattern consistent with IMNM
Liver biopsy: progression of NAFLD without autoimmune hepatitis—explains persistent transaminitis independent of myopathy
Excluding rhabdomyolysis/toxic myopathy: lack of severe acute CK spike at exposure, delayed CK rise over months, no cola-colored urine/myalgias, and lack of resolution with withdrawal alone

Causality assessment: application of WHO-UMC criteria—probable relationship given temporal association, lack of alternative explanations, and improvement after withdrawal plus immunotherapy; rationale against rechallenge

sections.description: Explains the therapeutic approach, monitoring, complications, and outcomes, emphasizing principles applicable to suspected drug-associated IMNM.
subtopics: Initial immunosuppression: IV methylprednisolone pulses followed by oral prednisone ~1 mg/kg
Adjunct therapy: IVIG 2 g/kg over 4 days for severe weakness/dysphagia
Monitoring response: rapid CK normalization over 2 weeks; functional recovery trajectory
Steroid taper: accelerated wean over ~2 months guided by strength and CK
Complications and mitigation: septic shock from pseudomonal UTI—risk recognition, infection surveillance while immunosuppressed
Cardiac follow-up: resolution of MRI abnormalities and arrhythmia; implications for screening in inflammatory myopathy
Medication stewardship: strict avoidance of GLP-1 receptor agonists; alternative strategies for obesity/NAFLD management
Long-term outcome: sustained remission off immunosuppression for months without relapse

sections.section_title: Clinical Pearls, Pitfalls, and Future Directions
sections.description: Synthesizes lessons for practice and outlines a pragmatic approach to patients on GLP-1 receptor agonists who develop weakness or CK elevation, along with research needs.
subtopics: When to suspect IMNM after GLP-1 RA exposure: progressive proximal weakness, dysphagia/dysphonia, rising CK over weeks to months
Early tests that change management: CK, myositis panel, thigh MRI, and timely muscle biopsy
Distinguishing toxic rhabdomyolysis from IMNM: kinetics of CK, symptom profile, and response to drug cessation
Seronegative IMNM is real: do not exclude diagnosis with negative antibodies; rely on clinicopathologic correlation
Treatment principles: prompt high-dose steroids and IVIG for severe bulbar involvement; individualized taper once CK and strength improve
Safety considerations: infection prophylaxis/monitoring, cardiac assessment, and patient education on red flags
Pharmacovigilance: report suspected cases; avoid rechallenge; discuss risks/benefits of GLP-1 RAs in patients with unexplained CK elevation or prior myopathy
Research gaps: mechanisms linking GLP-1 RAs to immune myopathy, genetic/predisposing factors, biomarkers to predict risk, and optimal therapy duration in drug-associated IMNM
